title: Sandwell Carers Service - AWARD
description:
ASC146 - Sandwell Carers Service
      
      The Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council wishes to procure a new Carers Service in Sandwell where carers can access information, advice, and support in line with the Care Act 2014.  
      
      The Care Act 2014 placed a duty on all Councils to consider the needs of carers on equal footing to the person receiving care and support. There is a clear focus in the Act on promoting carers' wellbeing, taking account of the impact caring has on all aspects of their lives. It is therefore a statutory requirement that every Council has a robust offer to identify carers and support them appropriately. 
      
      The new service will work with local partners towards better lives for Carers in Sandwell. It will improve outcomes for Sandwell carers, including health, wellbeing and opportunities. 
      
      Key functions will include: 
      1.	Support for carers to identify or be identified as carers - including campaigns, targeted activities for under- represented groups of carers and promotion/awareness raising
      2.	Single point of access for carers with information and advice, and signposting to the right support
      3.	Preventative community based support - including peer support groups and work with local partners
      4.	Checks on carer wellbeing
      5.	Wellbeing plans and triage to the right services as needed, including Adult Social Care and Children's Trust
      
      The successful contractor will be required to have responsibility for the delivery of the Service in compliance with legislation including the Care Act 2014, Children and Families Act 2014, and to support and empower carers to meet key outcomes. 
      
      Tenderers should note that:
      -	The Council has set the budget for the service, which is outlined in the Invitation to Tender documentation. 
      -	Subcontracting tenders are permitted, but a single lead provider is required to be responsible for managing the delivery of any subcontractors to meet the requirements of the Specification.
      
      The duration of the contract will be 5 years from 2 June 2025 to 1 June 2030.

description:
Provision of a Community Dementia Support Service
      
      Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council invites tenders for the provision of a Community Dementia Support Service to provide a range of support for people living with memory concerns and those living with the effects of dementia including carers.
      
      The Service will consist of a team of Dementia Navigators, Manager and administrative support, as a minimum. The Lead Provider is required to ensure an effective structure is in place to deliver the different elements of the Service Sandwell wide. 
      
      The Service will support the health, wellbeing and independence of those accessing the Service in community settings including care homes. The Service will provide support in acute settings to ensure appropriate information is provided in a timely manner following a diagnosis, crisis avoidance to prevent an inappropriate admission to hospital and timely discharge for people appropriately admitted to hospital. The Service will deliver training for professionals, communities and people living with the effects of dementia including carers and those with a memory concerns to enable them to become self-managing.
      
      The Service will be delivered on behalf of Sandwell MBC and the Black Country Integrated Care Board [BCICB] to support Sandwell citizens.

title: CWC24020 - Black Country Transport - Strategic Transport Review
description:
The Black Country Transport leads seek to commission a consultant to undertake an independent review of our capacity and capability to develop and deliver over the next 10 years in order to maximise the investment within the Black Country working alongside wider partners including Transport for West Midlands which is part of the West Midlands Combined Authority.\r
\r
The proposal is to commission a consultant, who can look at the area over a 2-3 month period in relation to the current setup, interfaces with maintenance capital expenditure and other partners to identify challenges objectively and make recommendations to mature the delivery function This would involve conducting a series of interviews at Director and Manager level across BCT and enabling services (finance, procurement etc), the 4 Local Authorities and key officers within WMCA/TfWM and group workshops to engage with officers involved in the day to day operational aspects of transport schemes\r
\r
City of Wolverhampton Council procures on behalf of Black Country Transport (BCT). BCT in any instance may represent City of Wolverhampton Council (CWC), Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council (SMBC), Walsall Council and Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council (DMBC) separately or in any combination of the four Local Authorities.\r
\r
BCT, formed of transportation officers from Dudley, Sandwell and Walsall Metropolitan Borough Councils and City of Wolverhampton Council, is a collaborative organisation which develops transportation projects across the Black Country region. As the lead authority, City of Wolverhampton Council runs procurement exercises on behalf of BCT, therefore, although projects are often schemes which are geographically situated across the Black Country, the contract will be entered into with City of Wolverhampton Council.

title: ASC130 Wrap Around Service  - AWARD
description:
Provision of a Wrap Around Service (ASC130) 
      
      Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council invites tenders for the provision of a Wrap Around Service. 
      
      The Council has committed with its health partners to provide a short-term Wrap Around Service to people who require care in their own home. This commitment is to ensure that people in the community are supported in their own homes to remain independent or to support a person being discharged from hospital who may need support whilst longer term arrangements are being established. The principle of the service is to ensure people's independence is maximised and individuals are not formally entered into the care and support system unnecessarily.
      
      The aim of the service is to promote a Home First ethos and support individuals to remain in their own homes by providing Care Workers at short notice, and within an hour of contact, to step in and prevent community crisis, and provide care and support to enable an assessment of an individual's needs, for up to 72 hours. This may include offering day and/or night sits to support a person for up to 72 hours.  The Wrap Around Service will enable people with or without assessed needs under the Care Act to have access to a short-term provision (up to 72 hours) to support them to continue to live independently in the community or prevent a hospital admission whilst longer term needs are being assessed.  
      
      Organisations with the capability to provide a service at short notice, and within an hour of contact, for extended periods where day or night sits may be required, are invited to tender.
      
      The total cost is estimated to be £457,531.20 per year subject to referrals being received that match predictions and any potential uplift in care costs.

title: Subscribed Garden Waste Stickers and Printing Capability - TBW061 - AWARD
description:
Subscribed Garden Waste Stickers and Printing Capability - TBW061
      
      Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council - subscribed garden waste collection service. Approved by Cabinet 16th November 2022, this scheme is to be introduced March 2023 with estimated 50,000 subscribers who will be identified from a sticker affixed to their 240L garden waste bin lid.
      It is anticipated the value will be in the region of £60,000 for 40,000 stickers
      The Key objectives/required outcomes are as follows:
      To provide a product (stickers) and printing portal capability to link with the Councils Whitespace system and to enable the portal to receive details of subscribers to the Councils garden waste collection service, no later than February 2023.
      To provide a product (stickers) with details of addresses and printing portal capability to receive a CSV or other mutually agreed format automatically from the Council's customer portal system so that supplier's system receives requests for new garden waste or replacement garden waste stickers on a daily basis.    
      To dispatch stickers by the end of the next working day and issue a despatch confirmation email to residents who have opted for this facility.  (GDPR issue passing the email address will need opt in/out box on portal form plus data agreement etc)
      The stickers will be used to enable collection crews to visually determine whether a property is subscribing to the Councils new garden waste collection scheme. It is intended to invite residents to subscribe to the new service in January/February to enable collection routes to be developed and residents added to the Councils waste management database Whitespace by early March 2023. 
      We anticipate that the majority of stickers will be requested in the run up and 3 months following the start of the garden waste collection in mid-March but we will still require a timely printing and despatch of new or replacement stickers throughout the garden waste collection year i.e., between March and December 2023.

Digital Autopsy/CT Scanning is used as first line intervention as an alternative to traditional post-mortem examinations within the Black Country. title: Developing the Sandwell Story and the Sandwell Strategic Partnership - AWARD
description:
Developing the Sandwell Story and the Sandwell Strategic Partnership
      
      Ref: CCS 001
      
      In the early 2000s, Sandwell had a local strategic partnership as was statutory for all local authorities at the time. This partnership developed a vision and a Sandwell Plan to guide partnership working and had a series of thematic groups sitting beneath it, leading on each aspect of the vision. A partnership director and their team supported these arrangements. 
      As the statutory requirement to have an LSP was taken away, this form of strategic partnership was dismantled (c.2009). In its place, separate thematic strategic partnerships continued (only those that were statutory) and the coherence of a single local strategic partnership was lost. 
       
      In 2015/16 work started to develop the current Vision 2030. This was developed in collaboration with the different thematic statutory partnerships and extensive consultation and engagement with other partners, staff, young people, residents and the voluntary/community sector took place. 
      Vision 2030 was adopted as the vision for Sandwell in 2017. The vision is made up of 10 ambitions - five ambitions relating to Sandwell's people and five relating to Sandwell, the place. No overall ownership of the Sandwell Vision was vested with any single partnership and subsequent political changes has meant that Vision 2030 drifted out of focus with partners.

description:
The Council wishes to invite applications for funding for the Adult Skills Programme from providers with a proven track record and, where applicable, an Ofsted rating of Good or Outstanding (see provider requirements and eligibility below).
      
      The contract and timescale for delivery will cover learners enrolling and undertaking learning from 1st August 2025 to 30th June 2026.  Delivery of provision must be completed by 30th June 2026. 
      
      Programmes are to be targeted at adults (aged over 19 on 31st August 2025) from one or more of the following groups:
      
      ? Adults who are unemployed.
      ? Adults who have been made recently redundant.
      ? Adults with no or low qualifications.
      ? Adults with low skills and no skills and who would benefit from taking a first step back into structured education and training.
      ? Adults with enduring mental ill health.
      ? Carers. 
      ? Homeless adults and adults living in hostel accommodation.
      ? Adults with learning difficulties/disabilities.
      ? Adults from ethnic minority groups.
      ? Male adults.
      ? Younger adults, aged 19 to 24 years.
      ? Older adults (usually 50+) who missed out on education when they were younger for various reasons.
      ? Newcomers into Sandwell facing specific barriers and experiencing significant disadvantages, reflecting local needs. 
      
      Courses should:
      
      ? Have clear learning aims that will result in adults being better prepared to move on to further learning, work or volunteering.
      ? Be delivered by tutors with appropriate subject qualifications who hold a minimum of a level 3 Award in Education and Training or equivalent. 
      ? Address local needs. 
      ? Address one or more of the Sandwell Adult and Family Learning Service commissioning priorities outlined in Annex A of the attached specification.
      ? Be delivered between 1st August 2025 and 30th June 2026.
      
      We expect activities to be in response to local needs and to deliver community-based learning activities. title: Toxicology Services  2024 - 2028 - AWARD
description:
Sandwell MBC (the "Council") is the relevant authority for the Black Country Coroners Jurisdiction which covers four local authority areas namely; Sandwell MBC, Dudley MBC, Walsall MBC and the City of Wolverhampton. Annually approximately 5000 deaths are reported to the Senior Coroner for the Black Country.  
      When discharging his or her judicial responsibilities, a coroner will make whatever inquiries are necessary when endeavouring to establish a cause of death. Those inquiries although not exclusively may involve a Digital Autopsy scan, a Post Mortem examination and in some instances the use of Toxicology Services to ensure that service he or she provides meets the needs of the bereaved in a timely manner. The Council is therefore co-ordinating a tender exercise for Toxicology Services and wishes to invite interested suppliers ("Tenderers") to participate in a tender exercise in relation to the supply of these services ("invitation to Tender" or "ITT").
